notes:
CIRCUIT: a 6-column x 5-row hand-drawn ladder/mesh of passive elements plus five sources on the top rail (V-AC 3V/1kHz, I-AC 5A/1kHz, V-DC 5V, I-DC 10A, V-DC 15V, left to right). Vertical columns at x~30, 197, 381, 568, 747, 943; horizontal rails at y~218 (sources), y~390 (50mH inductor + 100uF cap in line), y~555 (10uH inductor + 50uF cap in line), y~728 (5uH inductor + 10uF cap in line), y~900 (1uH inductor + 5uF cap in line). The drafter's convention on this sheet is explicit: every intended NON-connection is drawn as a downward semicircular hop, every intended connection is a T (often with a solder blob). 7 nets, 14 components, 27 terminals.

NET MAP:
 n1 = the whole left-hand column x~30, top rail corner down to the bottom-left corner: V-AC left (1.0), plus the left end of each of the three middle rails, i.e. 50mH left (8.0), 10uH left (6.0), 5uH left (3.0), and along the bottom 1uH left (0.0).
 n2 = column x~197, from the top rail between V-AC and I-AC straight down to the bottom rail at (201,910); rails y~390/555/728 all hop over it. Terminals: V-AC right (1.1), I-AC left (2.0), 1uH right (0.1), 5uF left plate (4.1).
 n3 = column x~381, from the solder dot on the top rail at (382,222) between I-AC and V-DC 5V, down to the dot at (382,725) on the y~728 rail; rails y~390 and y~555 hop over it. Terminals: I-AC right (2.1), V-DC 5V left (5.0), 5uH right (3.1), 10uF left plate (7.0).
 n4 = the right-hand column x~943 (top-rail right end down to the bottom-right corner) united with column x~568 through the y~728 rail. Path: V-DC 15V right (11.1) -> down x~943 -> S14 T with 100uF right (12.0) -> straight past S27 (crossing, see below) -> S41 T at (928,731) -> y~728 rail leftwards: 10uF right (7.1) and S43 T at (559,733) -> up column x~568 (hopping the y~555 and y~390 rails) to the top rail T at (571,221): V-DC 5V right (5.1) and I-DC left (9.0). The bottom rail right of the 5uF cap runs to (920,900) and turns up to the same S41 node, so 5uF right (4.0) is also n4. 6 terminals.
 n5 = the y~555 rail segment between the 10uH right lead and the 50uF left plate; it hops the x~568 column at S33. Terminals 6.1, 10.0.
 n6 = the y~390 rail segment between the 50mH right lead and the 100uF left plate; it hops the x~747 column at S23. Terminals 8.1, 12.1.
 0 = GND (13.0) and the y~540 rail running left from it, through the S27 crossing, to the 50uF right plate (10.1); column x~747 T-joins that rail at (740,551) and runs up (hopping y~390 at S23) to the top rail between I-DC and V-DC 15V: I-DC right (9.1), V-DC 15V left (11.0).

JUDGEMENT CALLS:
 * S27 (944,539) - the only genuinely ambiguous site. The y~540 rail crosses the right column at x=943 and continues ~25px further right into the long bar of the GND symbol. inkmap at (930,537) shows a 2px vertical and a 3px horizontal whose overlap widens to only 4px - no symmetric ~3x blob, so no solder dot; and no hop. Decided CROSSING. Rationale is electrical impossibility (BRIEF rule 1), not the ink prior: V-DC 15V has its LEFT terminal on column x~747, which T-joins this same y~540 rail at (740,551) with an unmistakable T (verified at 8x). Reading S27 as a junction would put both terminals of the 15V source on net 0 - a dead short across a voltage source - and would simultaneously put both terminals of the 10A I-DC source on net 0 (its left terminal reaches x~943 via column x~568 and the y~728 rail). The crossing reading leaves every source with two distinct nets. Expressed as explicit edge groups "27": [[40,63],[62,61]] rather than "crossing" because the site has degree 5 (the 3px GND stub e61 is counted twice) and I wanted the pairing pinned: e40 = column above, e63 = column below, e62 = rail to the left, e61 = stub into GND.
 * S33 (570,579) - the tracer defaulted to junction (hop score only 3.6) but at 8x this is an unmistakable semicircular hop: the y~555 rail dips below while the x~568 column runs straight through. OVERRIDDEN to crossing. Had it been a junction, n5 (10uH right + 50uF left) would have been absorbed into n4 and those two parts would have lost their own node; it would also have shorted the 10uH/50uF midpoint to the 5V and 10A source terminals.
 * S21 (571,414), S22 (380,418), S23 (747,418), S24 (195,427), S34 (380,583), S35 (196,585), S44 (196,745) - all identical downward semicircular hops of a horizontal rail over a vertical column; recorded as crossings (agreeing with the tracer). Reading any of them as a junction would merge two independent columns and collapse the mesh.
 * S6 (750,219), S7 (382,222), S8 (571,221), S14 (945,379), S20 (30,403), S28 (740,551), S32 (28,569), S39 (382,725), S41 (928,731), S42 (29,731), S43 (559,733), S50 (201,910) - all clean T-junctions (S7, S39, S42, S43 carry visible solder blobs); recorded as junctions explicitly, having inspected each crop.

PORT FIX:
 * Component #10 (50uF capacitor, in line in the y~555 rail with vertical plates): the tracer had bound t0 to p2@(661,510), which is the top tip of the left plate where the handwritten '50u' label stroke brushes the annotated box - that left net n5 with a single terminal. The real left lead is p1@(629,556). Fixed with ports {"10": {"0": 1, "1": 0}}; n5 now correctly has 2 terminals.

OTHER CHECKS:
 * All 14 classes confirmed against the drawn symbols (4 inductors as coils, 5 capacitors as parallel-plate pairs, 2 circled +/- V-DC, 2 circled arrow/sine sources, 1 GND). No class changes.
 * Every remaining tracer warning about 'unused port candidates' was traced to a stroke of the handwritten value/units label (3V, 1kHz, 5A, 5uH, 10uH, 10uF, 100uF, 50u, 15V) touching the component box; none of them is a real lead.
 * The 100uF, 50uF, 10uF and 5uF capacitors are all drawn with VERTICAL plates and sit in line in horizontal rails (not in vertical branches); confirmed at 6x zoom.
 * Nothing left unresolved.
